title: MCP fetch_batch Response
description: Serving-integrity contract U11/R15: `tools/mcp_server.py`'s `fetch_batch` tool response, built by `_serialize_batch_result`. U9 (R8-R11, R18, KD1, KD2): a server-planned, difficulty-laddered working set for one (student, skill) — every item's full rendered instance (KD6, nothing stripped), which ladder rung it fills, the submission context the double-diagnosis rule requires (orchestrator/batch.py's module docstring), and the shipped branching-policy object (KD2, KTD8). `batch-refill-result.schema.json` is this same family — a refill wraps this exact shape (nullable) with a signal/supersede envelope; that file duplicates the nested item/policy $defs below rather than cross-file $ref, matching this repo's existing single-file-$defs convention (schemas/item-record.schema.json).

instance.description: The full rendered item instance verbatim (KD6) — see schemas/item-instance.schema.json for its own complete, separately-validated shape; not re-validated field-by-field here.

rung.description: Which ladder rung this item fills (orchestrator/batch.py's plan_ladder).

context.description: The attempt-event context this item must be submitted under. "target"/"harder" rungs are always "practice"; "easier"/step-down rungs are always "probe" (the double-diagnosis fix, orchestrator/batch.py's module docstring) — the only two values plan_ladder ever assigns, a proper subset of attempt-event.schema.json's full context enum.

floor.description: The fallback sequence a client that doesn't recognize policy_version should use (KTD8).

low_water.description: The client-side signal for "ask for a refill soon" (KD2/R10) — not enforced server-side.

items.description: May hold fewer than count_requested if the candidate pool ran out (plan point e) — never padded with a repeat.

count_requested.description: The clamped batch_size actually planned against.

count_returned.description: len(items) — may be less than count_requested, never more.

feedback_sidecar.description: Every misconception_id reachable from any served distractor of any item in this batch, mapped to its child-facing feedback text (R18/AE8) — keyed by misconception_id.
